text:
olivia-cs: SableHarbor reports a sudden p99 embed latency spike starting ~09:12 UTC, from ~450ms to 6-8s; customer seeing timeouts in their nightly batch job. request_id=sh-req-0a9c. Can we get triage?
maria-support: Thanks — they said spike correlates with a campaign bulk embed run, ~120k requests over 5m. They hit our shared embeds pool.
infra-bot: [ALERT] embeddings-p99 > 5s cluster-wide at 2026-03-17T09:12:08Z. Top contributors: tenant=sableharbor (42%), tenant=driftly (8%).
zach-eng: @maria-support can you share sample headers and client concurrency? Also are they on reserved capacity or shared?
olivia-cs: Shared tier, API key mask sk-***a4. Concurrency ~100 workers from their side, controlled ramp but bursty at start.
devon-sre: I pulled traces for request_id=sh-req-0a9c — tail shows long queue wait before model invocation. Not pure GPU slowness, it's queuing/redis contention on prefix cache lookup.
amr: (typo, ignore)
sam-platform: Confirmed Redis client-side slow commands spikes at same window: many `MGET` and `EXPIRE` patterns. Evictions spiked.
zach-eng: That smells like noisy neighbor doing large prefix variations => cache miss storm, backend falls back to full KV recompute. Immediate mitigation: rate-limit per-tenant or route SableHarbor to a different pool.
maria-support: Customer asks for quickest fix — they want a temporary "fast lane" while we debug. Could we add a temporary reservation or bypass their requests from throttle?
devon-sre: Options: 1) Apply soft per-tenant concurrency cap (100 -> 30) in the proxy for shared pool; 2) Add a tenant-specific allowlist to bypass global circuit-breaker/routing so they go to a cold spare pool; 3) Short-term knob: increase Redis connection pool and bump cache TTL to avoid too many recomputes.
oncall-bot: @devon-sre acknowledged incident and paged oncall duty.
zach-eng: I can push a proxy rule to cap concurrency for tenant=sableharbor to 30. That should reduce tail and protect others. Will monitor. Command I used locally: `PATCH /proxy/rules` payload: `{ "match": "tenant:sableharbor", "concurrency_limit": 30, "ttl": 1800 }`
maria-support: Please confirm post-change impact window to communicate to customer.
zach-eng: Pushed at 09:20 UTC. Observability: `redwood.metrics.p99.embeds{tenant="sableharbor"}` dropped from 6.2s -> 520ms within 45s.
infra-bot: [METRIC] embeddings.p99(tenant:sableharbor) = 0.52s at 2026-03-17T09:20:45Z. Cluster-level p99 now 0.9s.
olivia-cs: Customer confirmed timeouts stopped and nightly job progressed, but they want a durable fix — asking for root cause and prevention.
devon-sre: Root cause: cache churn from high cardinality prompt prefixes + simultaneous warm requests causing backend recomputes and Redis pressure. Correlated with a large campaign. Log snippet: ```WARN cache: miss batch=924 keys=1200 tenant=sableharbor```.
sam-platform: Long-term fixes: - Suggest tenant-specific reservation or scheduled bulk window with Dedicated / reserved capacity. - Add per-tenant KV sharding so heavy tenants don't hot-spot a single Redis keyspace. - Autodetect bulk embed patterns and spill to background job with lower priority.
zach-eng: Also recommending they enable client-side batching where possible (batch_size=32) and prefix normalization. We'll offer a temporary promo for dedicated burst capacity if they want SLA.
maria-support: I'll draft an outbound to SableHarbor: summary + suggested mitigations (cap applied, propose reserved window or short-term dedicated burst, ask to try client batching).
olivia-cs: Next steps: 1) keep cap in place for 24h, 2) follow up with infra eng about Redis shard plan (sam/platform), 3) offer customer reserved burst trial.
sam-platform: Ack, filing infra task INF-4721 to evaluate tenant-aware sharding and cache TTL heuristics.
oncall-bot: Incident closed oncall rotation at 09:45 UTC (no active pager).
maria-support: Thanks everyone. I'll send update to SableHarbor and reopen if they see recurrence. :thumbsup:
